name: Phoenicia, Israel, Judah & Carthage
summary: While Phoenician sailors from Tyre and Byblos spread the 22-letter phonetic alphabet, purple dye, and founded Carthage in the western Mediterranean, the kingdoms of Israel and Judah composed the core texts of the Hebrew Bible (Tanakh).
keyFacts: Phoenician 22-consonant alphabet—ancestor of Greek, Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic, and Hebrew scripts
Compilation of the Hebrew Bible (Torah & Prophets)—foundation of Abrahamic monotheism
Circumnavigation of Africa under Phoenician mariners (~600 BCE)
